passed.title: Wrap plain columns in pl.struct before calling Expr.struct.json_encode
passed.trap: `Expr.struct.json_encode` exists only in the `.struct` namespace and only works on a Struct column. There is no top-level `json_encode` on `Expr`, and calling `.struct.json_encode()` on a plain column raises an error. To serialise several columns per row (a pandas `to_json(orient='records')` habit), first combine them with `pl.struct`, then call `Expr.struct.json_encode`. Null field values are written as JSON `null` and the key is kept, so downstream consumers must not assume missing keys mean null.
passed.example:
import polars as pl

df = pl.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": ["x", None]})

# Wrong: column 'a' is Int64, not a Struct
try:
    df.select(pl.col("a").struct.json_encode())
except Exception as e:
    print(type(e).__name__)

# Right: build a struct first, then encode it
out = df.select(pl.struct("a", "b").struct.json_encode().alias("json"))
print(out)
print(out["json"].to_list())
